findings.title: Second `downsize` overrides the first, so the emoji resize call now raises
findings.description:
`OptimizedImage` now defines `self.downsize` twice: the width/height form at lines 145-147 and the `dimensions` form at lines 149-151. In Ruby the later definition replaces the earlier one, so the width/height method is dead code. Any five-argument call raises `ArgumentError`.

`app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`. Every custom emoji upload therefore fails in that job. `Jobs::Base#perform` rescues the exception and passes it to `Discourse.handle_job_exception` (`app/jobs/base.rb:110-111`), so the failure is only reported. Emoji are never capped at 100x100, and `enforce_square_emoji` is not applied. No spec covers the emoji job, so this went unnoticed.

Fix: remove the duplicate and change the emoji call to pass `"100x100"`, or keep one method that accepts both forms.

findings.title: Existing JS test asserts the removed setting-based limit and will fail
findings.description: "prevents files that are too big from being uploaded" sets `max_image_size_kb = 5` and expects a 10 KB file to be rejected with `max_size_kb: 5`. After this change, `validateUploadedFile` compares against a hardcoded 10240 KB (`utilities.js:182-183`). The 10 KB file passes, `validUpload` returns true, and `not(validUpload([image]))` fails. The diff does not touch this test. Update it to the new boundary, or restore the setting-based check.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10 MB limit replaces the admin settings on the client and in the API path
findings.description:
`max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb` are `client: true` settings (`config/site_settings.yml:513-518`, default 3072 KB each). The client check used to read them. Now it uses `10 * 1024` at `utilities.js:182` and again at `utilities.js:246` (the 413 handler). The server uses `10.megabytes` at `uploads_controller.rb:55`.

- Admin attachment limits are no longer checked before upload. The server still enforces them (`lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:80-88`), so users only learn of the rejection after uploading.
- The upload selector still reads `max_attachment_size_kb` (`upload-selector.js.es6:17-18`), so client code now draws on two sources for the same limit.
- The default API URL download cap rises from 3 MB to 10 MB.
- The three literals duplicate one value. The 413 message also assumes a 10 MB nginx limit, which the admin controls.

Suggest one constant or setting shared between client and server, with the client keeping the setting it already uses for attachments.

findings.title: The reduction loop ignores failures and repeats the full pipeline
findings.description: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when convert fails (`convert_with`, `optimized_image.rb:160-169`), but the loop discards the return value and logs nothing. For a corrupt file or a non-image with an image extension, all five attempts run convert. Then `Upload.create_for` reports a generic "too large" error, and the real cause is lost. Break on failure and log it, for example `break unless OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` plus a `Rails.logger.warn`.

findings.title: Raster downsizing is applied to SVG and animated GIFs without the special cases used elsewhere
findings.description:
The guard uses `FileHelper.is_image?`, which includes `svg` (`lib/file_helper.rb:31`). Elsewhere, SVG is special-cased: `OptimizedImage.create_for` skips resizing it (`optimized_image.rb:45-47`), and `Upload.create_for` reads its dimensions with Nokogiri (`upload.rb:63-66`). The new loop instead runs ImageMagick `-resize` on the SVG and writes the output back to the `.svg` path. I did not verify what ImageMagick produces for SVG. It may rasterize or corrupt the vector file.

For animated GIFs, `"80%"` is passed to `resize_instructions_animated`, which uses it as gifsicle `--resize-fit` (`optimized_image.rb:115-124, 137-139`). I could not confirm that gifsicle accepts a percentage there. Exclude SVG from the loop, and confirm or replace the gifsicle geometry.

findings.title: New behavior has no test coverage
findings.description: The diff adds the reduction loop, a new `downsize` overload, and a 10 MB API download cap, but no spec changes. The controller spec has no oversized-image case. `spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb` covers only `create_for` and stubs `resize`. Nothing references `Jobs::ResizeEmoji`, which is why finding 1 is not caught. Add specs for: an oversized image reduced under the limit; an image still too large after five attempts; a failing convert; and the emoji job call.

findings.title: Removed `OptimizedImage.dimensions` has no remaining callers
findings.description: A repository search found no remaining uses of `dimensions(` on `OptimizedImage`, so removing it is safe. The numeric `resize` callers in `upload.rb:98`, `lib/letter_avatar.rb:48`, and `lib/tasks/uploads.rake:347` still work with the new `resize` body.
